q: The Jordan normal form of a matrix A decomposes A into blocks of the form λI + N where N is nilpotent. This matters for dynamics because:
opts: Nilpotent parts cause only polynomial growth, not exponential growth
Nilpotent parts are always zero in practice
Nilpotent parts correspond to complex eigenvalues
exp: Jordan blocks with λ on the diagonal give solutions like tᵏeλt — the nilpotent part N contributes polynomial factors. For stability analysis: if Re(λ)<0, polynomial×exponential decay still decays. If Re(λ)=0 and N≠0, polynomial growth occurs.
